back: The electrostatic attraction between two nuclei and a shared pair of electrons.
A covalent bond in which both shared electrons come from the same atom.
Energy needed to break one mole of a covalent bond in gaseous molecules (average value for bonds in different molecules).
NH₄⁺ (N → H⁺), H₃O⁺ (O → H⁺), Al₂Cl₆ (two Cl → Al bonds), ligands in complex ions.

front: Examples of expanded octets and odd-electron molecules?
back: Expanded: PCl₅ (10), SF₆ (12), SO₂. Odd electrons: NO (11), NO₂ (17).

front: How do bond length and bond energy compare for C–C, C=C, C≡C?
back: More shared pairs → shorter and stronger: C–C 350, C=C 610, C≡C 840 kJ mol⁻¹.
N≡N triple bond with a very high bond energy (944 kJ mol⁻¹), non-polar → high activation energy.
C–I is the weakest C–halogen bond (240 kJ mol⁻¹); bond strength outweighs polarity.
